title: The universal-low-basis proof applies ordinary low basis to a tree computable in the jump.
details: Cenzer–Remmel2017, Theorem3.1.4(b) proof p97, visually checked. The amalgamation tree tests whether each Pi01 class is nonempty and is only shown computable in0-prime. Applying the preceding low-basis construction to that oracle-computable tree does not produce a member low over the empty oracle; relativization would give a jump bound relative to0-prime instead. The stated universal-low-degree conclusion is not justified by this inference. A repair for computably bounded classes is to use a computable universal binary DNC/separator class: every path computes a member of every nonempty computable binary-tree class, and ordinary low basis supplies a low member of that computable universal class. Computably bounded finite alphabets can be effectively encoded in binary. This adjacent argument is excluded from adoption.
